title: The animal that survived open space

lines.text: There's an animal smaller than a grain of sand that survived being sent into space.
Meet the tardigrade, also called the water bear.
Most are under half a millimetre long.
When things get bad, it dries out into a ball called a tun, and its metabolism stops.
In that state, it can briefly survive from about minus 272 to plus 149 degrees Celsius.
In 2007, scientists strapped dried tardigrades to a satellite, and exposed them to space for 10 days.
The vacuum alone didn't kill them. Some even survived the harsh solar UV.
They can go years without water, and carry a protein that helps shield their DNA.
If anything outlives us on this planet, it might be the water bear.

sources.claim: Tardigrades (water bears): usually ~0.5 mm; tun state halts metabolism; survive about −272 to +149 °C briefly; 2007 FOTON-M3: 10 days in space, vacuum alone harmless, some survived UV; Dsup protein protects DNA
